chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub Abu al-Hasan al-Ja'fi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from al-Mufaddal ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Hurayz, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, that he said:
When the Qa'im arises, Allah will remove the ailment from every believer and restore to him his strength.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the health and strength of believers when Imam al-Mahdi appears?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights a specific eschatological sign where the advent of Imam al-Mahdi brings about a physical restoration for believers, removing chronic ailments ('ahat') and renewing their vigor. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not merely as a miraculous healing but as a divine preparation, ensuring the faithful are physically robust to support the global establishment of justice. This physical renewal complements the spiritual purification associated with the Occultation's end, reinforcing the holistic nature of the Mahdist era.
